title: Find senior earners
description: Return each employee's name and salary when their salary is greater than 100,000. Sort from highest to lowest.
hint: Filter with WHERE, then sort the selected rows with ORDER BY.

expectedResult.query: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > 100000 ORDER BY salary DESC

solution:
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees
WHERE salary > 100000
ORDER BY salary DESC;

title: Find unassigned employees
description: Return the id and name of employees who do not belong to a department.
hint: NULL needs a special comparison. Use IS NULL instead of = NULL.

expectedResult.query: SELECT id, name FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NULL

title: Order the lowest salaries
description: Show the three lowest-paid employees. Return name and salary, from lowest to highest.
hint: ORDER BY salary ASC puts the smallest value first. LIMIT keeps only the first three rows.

expectedResult.query: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary ASC LIMIT 3

solution:
SELECT name, salary
FROM employees
ORDER BY salary ASC
LIMIT 3;

title: Show Engineering teammates
description: Return the employee name and department name for Engineering employees earning over 95,000.
hint: Join employees to departments using department_id, then filter the joined rows.

expectedResult.query: SELECT e.name, d.name AS department_name FROM employees AS e INNER JOIN departments AS d ON e.department_id = d.id WHERE d.name = 'Engineering' AND e.salary > 95000 ORDER BY e.name

solution:
SELECT e.name, d.name AS department_name
FROM employees AS e
INNER JOIN departments AS d ON e.department_id = d.id
WHERE d.name = 'Engineering' AND e.salary > 95000
ORDER BY e.name;

title: Review large pending orders
description: Return the id and amount for pending orders over 9,000.
hint: Both conditions belong in WHERE. Combine them with AND.

expectedResult.query: SELECT id, amount FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending' AND amount > 9000

title: Summarize order statuses
description: For each order status, show the number of orders and the total non-NULL amount.
hint: Group by status, then use COUNT(*) and SUM(amount).

expectedResult.query: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(amount) AS total_amount FROM orders GROUP BY status

title: Find departments with multiple people
description: Show department names and employee counts for departments with at least two employees. Sort by count from highest to lowest, then by department name.
hint: HAVING filters grouped counts after GROUP BY. WHERE cannot filter COUNT(*).

expectedResult.query: SELECT d.name AS department_name, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count FROM departments AS d INNER JOIN employees AS e ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name HAVING COUNT(e.id) >= 2 ORDER BY employee_count DESC, department_name ASC

solution:
SELECT d.name AS department_name, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count
FROM departments AS d
INNER JOIN employees AS e ON e.department_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name
HAVING COUNT(e.id) >= 2
ORDER BY employee_count DESC, department_name ASC;

title: Include empty departments
description: List every department and its employee count, including departments with no employees. Sort by count from highest to lowest, then name.
hint: Start from departments and LEFT JOIN employees. COUNT(e.id) returns zero for an unmatched department.

expectedResult.query: SELECT d.name AS department_name, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count FROM departments AS d LEFT JOIN employees AS e ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name ORDER BY employee_count DESC, department_name ASC

solution:
SELECT d.name AS department_name, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count
FROM departments AS d
LEFT JOIN employees AS e ON e.department_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name
ORDER BY employee_count DESC, department_name ASC;

title: Total completed order value by employee
description: Show employees with completed orders and their total completed order amount. Keep only totals over 10,000 and sort from highest to lowest.
hint: Join orders to employees, filter completed rows with WHERE, then GROUP BY the employee.

expectedResult.query: SELECT e.name, SUM(o.amount) AS completed_total FROM employees AS e INNER JOIN orders AS o ON o.employee_id = e.id WHERE o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY e.id, e.name HAVING SUM(o.amount) > 10000 ORDER BY completed_total DESC

solution:
SELECT e.name, SUM(o.amount) AS completed_total
FROM employees AS e
INNER JOIN orders AS o ON o.employee_id = e.id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY e.id, e.name
HAVING SUM(o.amount) > 10000
ORDER BY completed_total DESC;

title: Compare department salary averages
description: Show each department whose average salary is above 90,000. Return department name and average salary, highest average first.
hint: Join employees to departments, group by the department, and use HAVING AVG(salary) > 90000.

expectedResult.query: SELECT d.name AS department_name, AVG(e.salary) AS average_salary FROM employees AS e INNER JOIN departments AS d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.id, d.name HAVING AVG(e.salary) > 90000 ORDER BY average_salary DESC

solution:
SELECT d.name AS department_name, AVG(e.salary) AS average_salary
FROM employees AS e
INNER JOIN departments AS d ON e.department_id = d.id
GROUP BY d.id, d.name
HAVING AVG(e.salary) > 90000
ORDER BY average_salary DESC;
